_why: od9 does not use the ecosystem's crons/ convention — its scheduled scripts live under api/drip/, which is why this linter reported 'scanned 0 cron(s) — CLEAN' for the whole time it existed. A gate reading a directory this repo does not have is green for the wrong reason.
_duplicate_sender_finding: RESOLVED 2026-09-01: api/drip/processor.php is RETIRED. It was a second implementation of sender.php's job — both selected due enrollments, sent, logged to od9_drip_log and advanced the step — and it could never have worked: its query named four columns that do not exist (e.id, e.sequence_id, s.id, st.id; the real ones are enrollment_id, sequence_name, sequence_id, step_id). Scheduling it briefly on 2026-09-01 made it log exactly that. Note it was ALSO the file commit 206acb6 had just fixed, so 'most recently maintained' pointed confidently at the broken one; the live schema was the signal that settled it. Nothing was lost by deleting it: its only distinct behaviour was resolving a recipient from od9_members at send time, and event_processor.php already does that at ENROLMENT time (priority chain ending in od9_members.patreon_email) and stores the result on the row, which is what sender.php reads.
_extra_cron_globs_note: Listed one by one rather than as api/drip/*.php on purpose. That directory also holds webhook.php, which is a WEB endpoint reached by Square and Discord and must not have a CLI guard, and webhook_secret.config.php, which is configuration. Globbing the directory would flag both for 'no CLI guard' — a false positive on the very first run is how a gate loses its audience. All three are CLI cron scripts and each opens with php_sapi_name() !== 'cli'. Two of them are currently SCHEDULED in tools/crontab.offda9.txt (sender, event_processor); weekly_lovelogic_sender.php is not, and is linted anyway because the contract has to hold before something is scheduled, not after.
_crontab_note: tools/crontab.offda9.txt is now committed, so the cross-reference against prod's real schedule runs here — the check that caught cred-drift-monitor running repo-orphaned for 7 weeks. It reads every crontab line whose script path starts with the prefix and asserts the repo actually contains that file, which is what turns 'the crontab and the repo agree' from an assumption into a per-deploy claim. The earlier note said committing this file was the obvious next improvement; scheduling the drip on 2026-09-01 made it possible, because until then offda9 had no crontab at all.
